contextual.summary: Cardiff treats you as a contextual applicant if you answer yes to any of its UCAS-form circumstances (or complete one of its access programmes), or if a weighted score of area, school and parental-education data reaches 100, and then usually gives a lower offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: One or two grades below the standard offer (typically the middle to lower end of the advertised grade range)

criteria.detail: Care leaver or care experienced (e.g. lived in public care, foster care, kinship care or a residential children's home)
A parent or have parenting responsibilities (including pregnant, adopting, or a guardian or foster carer of a child)
Currently receiving, or received/eligible for, free school meals during secondary education
Have caring responsibilities (unpaid care for a family member or friend with an illness, disability, mental health condition or addiction)
Official refugee status in the UK, an asylum seeker, or limited leave to remain (also Ukraine scheme arrivals)
Estranged from both parents (not in contact with and supported by either of them)

Completed Cardiff's Confident Futures or Step Up to University (or Sutton Trust Medicine and Dentistry Summer Schools, Pathways to Engineering, Pathways to Law), or at another university Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking and Finance (including online), Engineering or Law; applying in the same year or the year after
POLAR4 (how likely young people in your area are to go to higher education): living in a low-participation area earns points towards your contextual score
Welsh, English, Scottish and Northern Irish indices of multiple deprivation for your home postcode: more deprived areas earn more points
DWP average household gross annual earnings for your home postcode: lower average earnings earn more points
Welsh and English sixth form performance data and free school meal rates for your school's postcode
Parents or guardians do not have a higher education qualification such as a degree (collected on the UCAS form)

contextual.rulesText: You are classed as contextual if you answer yes to any of the listed UCAS-form questions or complete one of the listed access activities. Otherwise Cardiff adds weighted points for area (POLAR4, deprivation indices, average household earnings), school (sixth form performance, free school meal rates) and parents without a degree into a score from 0-330: 0-99 is non-contextual and 100 or above signals disadvantage. Only information in the original UCAS application is used. Most applicants are not classed as contextual.

source.evidence: You will be classed as contextual if, on your UCAS application, you answer yes to any of the following questions ... be given an offer made at one or two grades lower than the standard offer

programmes.name: Step Up Summer School
programmes.summary: A free three-day residential summer school at Cardiff University for 16-17 year olds from under-represented backgrounds, with university-life sessions and taster lectures, including a Law, Politics and Business strand.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students aged 16-17 who live in Wales (Welsh postcode), attend a state-funded non-fee-paying school or college, have five GCSEs at A*-C including English and Maths, and meet at least one widening participation criterion.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Required: live in Wales with a Welsh postcode; attend (and have always attended) a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college; be 16 or 17 and in the first year of college (level 4) or sixth form (Year 12); have at least five GCSEs at A*-C including at least a C in English Language or Literature and Maths; and meet at least one additional criterion: live in an area where few people go to university or with high deprivation, be or have been in care, qualify for free school meals, be among the first generation of your family to attend university, be an asylum seeker or refugee, attend a school or college performing below the national average at Key Stage 4/5, be a young carer, be disabled, be an estranged young person, have a household income under £35,000, or be eligible for Education Maintenance Allowance. The more additional criteria you meet, the more likely you are to get a place.
benefits: Free to attend, including all meals and travel to and from Cardiff University campus
Stay in university halls and attend taster lectures, including subject-specific activities in Law, Politics and Business
Support with personal statements and budgeting
Completing Step Up to University means Cardiff classes you as a contextual applicant (usually an offer one or two grades lower)
programmes.offerReduction: Classed as a contextual applicant: usually an offer one or two grades lower than the standard offer (typically the middle to lower end of the advertised grade range)
programmes.subjects: All subjects (subject strands: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Law, Politics and Business; Medicine, Dentistry and Healthcare Sciences; Engineering, Mathematics and Physical Sciences)

runs.text: Three days in summer (2027 dates not published)

opens.text: Usually April to May (2027 date not published)

programmes.infoNote: Cardiff publishes no dated round for 2027: the page only says applications are 'usually open between April and May', so the opening time is an expectation based on that. The contextual admissions page lists 'Step Up to University' as a qualifying programme; the Step Up pages don't say whether the summer school and the masterclasses both count.

source.evidence: This opportunity is free to attend, including all meals whilst you are with us and travel to and from Cardiff University campus before, during and after the summer school.

notConfirmed: runs: summer 2027 dates not published

programmes.name: Step Up Masterclasses (Business, Accounting and Economics)
programmes.summary: A series of six academic masterclasses at Cardiff University for 16-17 year olds from under-represented backgrounds, with a Business, Accounting and Economics subject option.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students aged 16-17 who live in Wales (Welsh postcode) within 90 minutes of Cardiff University, attend a state-funded non-fee-paying school or college, have five GCSEs at A*-C including English and Maths, and meet at least one widening participation criterion.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Required: live in Wales with a Welsh postcode; attend (and have always attended) a state-funded, non-fee-paying school or college; be 16 or 17 and in the first year of college (level 4) or sixth form (Year 12); have at least five GCSEs at A*-C including at least a C in English Language or Literature and Maths; and meet at least one additional criterion: live in an area where few people go to university or with high deprivation, be or have been in care, qualify for free school meals, be among the first generation of your family to attend university, be an asylum seeker or refugee, attend a school or college performing below the national average at Key Stage 4/5, be a young carer, be disabled, be an estranged young person, have a household income under £35,000, or be eligible for Education Maintenance Allowance. The more additional criteria you meet, the more likely you are to get a place. For the masterclasses only: you must also live within 90 minutes of Cardiff University.
benefits: Six academic masterclasses in your chosen subject, including Business, Accounting and Economics
Insight into university learning and teaching and an experience to add to UCAS applications

courses.notes: Cardiff also offers Business Management with Marketing, Supply Chain Management, International Management and Welsh as separate courses. No required A-level subject, but GCSE Maths grade B/6 is needed unless you take A-level Maths.

notes: All six courses are taught by Cardiff Business School (Colum Road, Cathays, in the Cathays Park area of the city) and all ask for AAB-BBB at A-level.

Economics, Business Economics and Banking and Finance require A-level Maths. Economics and Management, Accounting and Finance and Business Management have no required A-level subject but ask for GCSE Maths grade B/6 unless you take A-level Maths.
The advertised AAB-BBB range covers the standard and contextual offers; a grade A in the EPQ typically earns an offer one grade lower than the standard offer.
Cardiff's Step Up programmes (including Business, Accounting and Economics masterclasses) are only open to students living in Wales with a Welsh postcode.
Halls rents (2026/27) start from about £131.81 to £186.76 a week depending on the hall (40-week contracts); 2027/28 prices will be available from May 2027.
Every course also has a 4-year version with a professional placement year under its own UCAS code.
